title: but pr new --single: publish ONLY the named branch (no ancestor pushes/reviews, no native stack registration) — the agent/automation PR path
description:
OUR FORK'S FEATURE #1 (from fabro-75fb, relocated here as the tracker of record; user directive 2026-10-03: fork + build ourselves, 'genau so wie mit seeds und mulch').

PROBLEM (verified in fabro, PR #369/#370/#372 incident): `but pr new` on a stacked branch pushes the branch AND its ancestors and creates reviews bottom-up — collateral ancestor PRs appear (e.g. line-branch -> frozen-base PRs, the hazard class our gates exist for). Additionally GitButler registers NATIVE GitHub stack metadata on its PRs; on GitHub instances without the async stacked-merge endpoint this BLOCKS every merge path (sync merge refused 'part of a stack', async REST 404s).

CODE SURFACE (located): crates/but/src/command/legacy/forge/review.rs — (a) but_api::legacy::workspace::workspace_branch_and_ancestors_push_only (line ~658) = the ancestor push+review walk; (b) sync_review_stack_after_review_creation (line ~719) = native stack registration; (c) ~line 322 'stacked publication try to recreate a dependency review' = dependency-review recreation. No configuration surface exists (feature flags: only unapply-v3-pgm + single-branch; neither touches PR creation) — verified 2026-10-03.

FEATURE: `--single` flag on `but pr new` (plus a persistent default, e.g. `but config feature pr-single enable`):
- publish ONLY the named branch: no ancestor pushes, no ancestor reviews, no dependency-review recreation;
- skip native stack metadata registration for that review entirely (plain branch PR);
- stacking stays the DEFAULT behavior for interactive use — single is the agent/automation path.

ACCEPTANCE: a stacked two-lane workspace (line + feature lane above) where `but pr new <feature> --single` creates EXACTLY ONE PR (for the feature branch, against its true base), pushes no other refs, registers no stack metadata, and the PR merges through the normal sync path. Tests: CLI flag parsing + the workspace publication path (the review.rs flow) with a fixture workspace; exit unchanged for default invocations.

evidence.tests: but-workspace/but-settings/but-api: 772/772 pass; but: 1936/1941 (5 fails = pre-existing WSL drvfs EACCES artifact, 1 proven on clean master); new: PushScope::BranchOnly behavioral push tests, chain short-circuit on stacked fixture, --single parse, pr-single config round-trip via real binary, prSingle settings serde+persist

closeReason: Implemented and landed via PR #1 (merge b2267789b4): --single publishes exactly one review, pushes no ancestor refs, skips stack registration; pr-single persistent default. Tests green (evidence in extensions).

title: fork release pipeline: v* tag -> but CLI binaries + SHASUMS -> GitHub Release (consumer mise pins switch to fork artifacts)
description:
OUR FORK'S DELIVERY PIPELINE (companion to the --single feature seed; mirrors denkhaus/seeds release conventions — seeds-6475/e160 pattern).

GOAL: ship our own `but` builds so every repo can pin OUR fork (the rollout gate: no repo joins GitButler until this exists).

DESIGN: GitHub Actions on this fork — v* tag -> build the but CLI (cargo build --release -p but) -> linux x86_64 artifact (+ aarch64 if cheap) + SHASUMS.txt -> GitHub Release. Keep tracking upstream main (remote 'upstream' is wired); merges deliberate, like petri/pebble forks in fabro.

CONSUMER SIDE (after first release): switch the mise http:but pins (fabro/.mise.toml, seeds, mulch + global ~/.config/mise/config.toml) from releases.gitbutler.com URLs to our fork's release artifact URLs; version scheme: start fork-local (e.g. 0.22.3-fork.1) so upstream-version collisions stay impossible.

ACCEPTANCE: tag -> release workflow green -> artifact downloadable + checksum-clean -> `mise install http:but` against the new URL resolves and `but --version` reports the fork version in a fresh shell.

evidence.note: workflow green run + artifact download/checksum verification pending the first tag

closeReason: Pipeline landed via PR #1 (merge b2267789b4). First tag v0.22.3-fork.1 proposed; release-run verification happens with the tag (coordinator confirmation pending).

title: fork-release: stamp CHANNEL=release so the fork binary uses the standard com.gitbutler.app app-data path
description: Found by the coordinator after v0.22.3-fork.1: our fork-release.yaml build job does not set CHANNEL, so crates/but/build.rs defaults IDENTIFIER to com.gitbutler.app.dev. The released fork binary therefore looks for its project registry and app data under ~/.local/share/com.gitbutler.app.dev instead of the standard com.gitbutler.app path that every upstream but install and the GUI use (crates/but/src/lib.rs:307, crates/but-path/src/lib.rs AppChannel::new). The coordinator bridged locally with a symlink. FIX: set CHANNEL=release in the build job env of .github/workflows/fork-release.yaml (build.rs maps release -> com.gitbutler.app). Takes effect from the next tag (v0.22.3-fork.2 onward); v0.22.3-fork.1 binaries keep the dev identity.

evidence.change: CHANNEL=release added to fork-release.yaml build env; build.rs maps release -> com.gitbutler.app
evidence.verification: takes effect from v0.22.3-fork.2 onward: first green fork.2 release run should show the standard app-data path; fork.1 keeps dev identity

closeReason: Landed via 51e0e166a2 on master: CHANNEL=release in the build env. Effect verifiable from the next release tag (fork.2); coordinator symlink bridge stays until then.
